successCriteria.description: The PgLeavePolicyRepository class implements all 6 methods of ILeavePolicyRepository (findById, findByLeaveType, findAll, create, update, delete) and each method compiles without type errors against the interface.
All SQL queries in PgLeavePolicyRepository use parameterized queries ($1, $2, ...) — no string concatenation or template interpolation of user-supplied values into SQL text.
The barrel export file (src/modules/leave-policy/index.ts) re-exports LeavePolicy, ILeavePolicyRepository, and PgLeavePolicyRepository as its public surface.
The repository imports the shared pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts (not creating its own pool or direct pg.Client).

Row-to-entity mapping converts snake_case column names (policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at) to camelCase LeavePolicy fields, and string timestamps to Date objects.

Unit tests exist at tests/unit/modules/leave-policy/leave-policy.repository.test.ts that mock the db pool and cover: findById returns a policy or null, findByLeaveType returns a policy or null, findAll returns all policies, create inserts and returns a new policy with generated id/timestamps, update modifies and returns the policy or null if not found, delete returns true/false based on row count.

constraints: All database access MUST go through the repository pattern (GP-001). The PgLeavePolicyRepository is the sole class that executes SQL against the leave_policies table — no other module or file may query leave_policies directly.
The repository MUST use the shared pool exported from src/shared/db/connection.ts. It MUST NOT create its own pg.Pool, pg.Client, or any other database connection.

The LeavePolicy entity fields MUST match the reconciled architecture exactly: id (string), policyName (string), leaveType (LeaveType from shared/types), entitlementDays (number), accrualRate (number | null), maxAccumulation (number | null), minimumNoticeDays (number | null), requiresManagerApproval (boolean), isActive (boolean), createdAt (Date), updatedAt (Date). No extra fields, no missing fields.
The repository MUST NOT use TypeScript `any`. Use `unknown` with type guards where the type is genuinely unknown. The LeavePolicyRow interface already provides a typed row shape — use it.
outOfScope: HTTP routes, controllers, Fastify registration, or any API surface for leave-policy — deferred to Phase 7 (LeaveService & API surface).
Database migration for the leave_policies table — the table is assumed to already exist with columns matching the snake_case names used in the repository's SQL queries.
Audit logging from the repository layer — GP-002 audit records are produced by the service/orchestrator layer (Phase 7), not by repository methods directly.
RBAC enforcement on leave-policy operations — policy CRUD is an HR-admin concern enforced at the controller/route layer in Phase 7.

entityInvariants.invariant: A LeavePolicy row MUST have a non-null, unique id (UUID v4 generated on create). The leaveType field MUST be one of the canonical LeaveType enum values from src/shared/types/index.ts. The isActive field governs the ACTIVE ↔ INACTIVE lifecycle; deactivating a policy (isActive: false) will freeze all associated LeaveBalances (enforced at the service layer in Phase 7).

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns null when no row matches the given id — does not throw. Database connectivity errors propagate as exceptions (no silent swallowing).

Returns null when no policy exists for the given leaveType — does not throw. Returns the first matching row if multiple exist (unique constraint on leave_type is expected but not enforced by the repository).
